claim: High-resolution template matching can localize ribosomes in two-dimensional electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) images of untilted Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells with high precision.
source: Previously, we showed that high-resolution template matching can localize ribosomes in two-dimensional electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) images of untilted Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells with high precision (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Lucas et al., 2021).

claim: Comparing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) observed with 2DTM using different templates relative to the same cellular target can correct for local variation in noise.
source: Here, we show that comparing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) observed with 2DTM using different templates relative to the same cellular target can correct for local variation in noise and differentiate related complexes in focused ion beam (FIB)-milled cell sections.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and analysis presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figures 2-6.

claim: Comparing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) observed with 2DTM using different templates relative to the same cellular target can differentiate related complexes in focused ion beam (FIB)-milled cell sections.
source: Here, we show that comparing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) observed with 2DTM using different templates relative to the same cellular target can correct for local variation in noise and differentiate related complexes in focused ion beam (FIB)-milled cell sections.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing differentiation of 60S intermediates in FIB-milled yeast cells.

claim: A maximum likelihood approach can define the probability of each particle belonging to each class, thereby establishing a statistic to describe the confidence of classification.
source: We use a maximum likelihood approach to define the probability of each particle belonging to each class, thereby establishing a statistic to describe the confidence of our classification.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methodology described in the manuscript and demonstrated in Figure 3.

claim: The method can separate the nuclear pre-60S population from the cytoplasmic mature 60S population, using the subcellular localization to validate assignment.
source: In the first, we separate the nuclear pre-60S population from the cytoplasmic mature 60S population, using the subcellular localization to validate assignment.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Relative 2DTM SNRs can be used to separate mixed populations of nuclear pre-60S that are not visually separable.
source: In the second, we show that relative 2DTM SNRs can be used to separate mixed populations of nuclear pre-60S that are not visually separable.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: 2DTM can distinguish related molecular populations without the need to generate 3D reconstructions from the data to be classified.
source: 2DTM can distinguish related molecular populations without the need to generate 3D reconstructions from the data to be classified, permitting classification even when only a few target particles exist in a cell.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methodology and results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: 2DTM permits classification even when only a few target particles exist in a cell.
source: 2DTM can distinguish related molecular populations without the need to generate 3D reconstructions from the data to be classified, permitting classification even when only a few target particles exist in a cell.
evidence: The claim is supported by the demonstration that classification can be performed on populations of <500 molecules.

claim: Cryo-EM enables simultaneous visualization of all cellular molecules in their native cellular environment while preserving high-resolution molecular architecture.
source: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) enables simultaneous visualization of all cellular molecules in their native cellular environment while preserving high-resolution molecular architecture.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cryo-EM capabilities.

claim: The high density of molecules in a cell and the low signal-to-noise ratio of cryo-EM micrographs make it difficult to identify molecules of interest.
source: However, realizing this promise is limited by the high density of molecules in a cell, and the low signal-to-noise ratio of cryo-EM micrographs, making it difficult to identify molecules of interest (Lučič et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Lučič et al., 2013).

claim: Electron cryo-tomography (cryo-ET) can be used to build 3D maps of cellular structures in their native context by reconstructing tomograms from a series of images of tilted 2D samples.
source: To address this, electron cryo-tomography (cryo-ET) can be used to build 3D maps of cellular structures in their native context (in situ) by reconstructing tomograms from a series of images of tilted 2D samples (Kürner et al., 2005; Lučič et al., 2013; Mahamid et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kürner et al., 2005; Lučič et al., 2013; Mahamid et al., 2016).

claim: Subtomogram averaging can yield in situ molecular structures at <4 Å resolution.
source: Once identified, subtomogram averaging can yield in situ molecular structures at <4 Å resolution (Himes and Zhang, 2018; Tegunov et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Himes and Zhang, 2018; Tegunov et al., 2021).

claim: The effective resolution of a raw tomogram is below 15–20 Å.
source: However, since the effective resolution of a raw tomogram is below 15–20 Å (Vilas et al., 2020), identification of specific targets in tomograms is limited to abundant particles that are sufficiently distinct at this resolution to be identified.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Vilas et al., 2020).

claim: Identification of specific targets in tomograms is limited to abundant particles that are sufficiently distinct at 15-20 Å resolution to be identified.
source: However, since the effective resolution of a raw tomogram is below 15–20 Å (Vilas et al., 2020), identification of specific targets in tomograms is limited to abundant particles that are sufficiently distinct at this resolution to be identified.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the resolution limitation of tomograms.

claim: 3D classification of subtomograms can differentiate between structural states.
source: 3D classification of subtomograms can differentiate between structural states (Himes and Zhang, 2018; Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Himes and Zhang, 2018; Xue et al., 2021).

claim: The assignment of states is unreliable for similar structures that can only be distinguished using high-resolution detail.
source: However, the assignment of states is unreliable for similar structures that can only be distinguished using high-resolution detail, and statistical approaches to quantitatively assess classification results are lacking.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the limitations of current methods.

claim: Statistical approaches to quantitatively assess classification results are lacking.
source: However, the assignment of states is unreliable for similar structures that can only be distinguished using high-resolution detail, and statistical approaches to quantitatively assess classification results are lacking.
evidence: The claim is based on assessment of the current state of the field.

claim: Machine learning has been employed for particle classification in tomograms, but currently only performs as well as a human operator.
source: Machine learning has been employed for particle classification in tomograms, but currently only performs as well as a human operator (Moebel et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Moebel et al., 2021).

claim: Machine learning algorithms perform better than 3D template matching at molecule localization in tomograms, but classification remains challenging for all algorithms.
source: While machine learning algorithms perform better than 3D template matching at molecule localization in tomograms, classification remains challenging for all algorithms (Gubins et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Gubins et al., 2020).

claim: 2DTM uses molecular models from in vitro structure determination or in silico structure prediction to generate a 3D density.
source: 2DTM uses molecular models, from in vitro structure determination or in silico structure prediction (e.g. Alphafold2 Jumper et al., 2021) to generate a 3D density.
evidence: The claim describes the methodology of 2DTM and cites Alphafold2 as an example (Jumper et al., 2021).

claim: 2DTM calculates millions of 2D projections representing different orientations of the molecule.
source: This 3D density (hereafter referred to as the template) is then used to calculate millions of 2D projections representing different orientations of the molecule.
evidence: The claim describes the 2DTM methodology.

claim: A pixel-wise cross-correlation of the 2D projections with a high-resolution 2D cryo-EM image is performed, yielding a 2DTM signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the best matching projection at every pixel location.
source: A pixel-wise cross-correlation of the 2D projections with a high-resolution 2D cryo-EM image is performed, yielding a 2DTM signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the best matching projection at every pixel location (Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim describes the 2DTM methodology and is supported by a citation (Rickgauer et al., 2017).

claim: The 2DTM SNR values are subjected to a significance test by comparison to a Gaussian noise distribution following a matched filter.
source: The 2DTM SNR values are subjected to a significance test by comparison to a Gaussian noise distribution following a matched filter, which is used to establish a threshold allowing a given number of false positives (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim describes the 2DTM methodology and is supported by citations (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2017).

claim: The 2DTM SNR is proportional to template mass.
source: The 2DTM SNR is proportional to template mass and negatively affected by non-matching elements between template and target (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).

claim: The 2DTM SNR is negatively affected by non-matching elements between template and target.
source: The 2DTM SNR is proportional to template mass and negatively affected by non-matching elements between template and target (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).

claim: A template generated from a Bacillus subtilis 50S large ribosomal subunit was able to detect 50S in 2D cryo-EM images of Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells, but with a lower average 2DTM SNR compared to a M. pneumoniae 50S template.
source: We have shown that a template generated from a Bacillus subtilis 50S large ribosomal subunit was able to detect 50S in 2D cryo-EM images of Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells, but with a lower average 2DTM SNR compared to a M. pneumoniae 50S template (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Lucas et al., 2021).

claim: 2DTM using partially matching templates can be sufficiently sensitive to yield significant targets.
source: This demonstrated that (1) 2DTM using partially matching templates can be sufficiently sensitive to yield significant targets and (2) the mean 2DTM SNR of detected targets provides a read-out of the relative similarity between different templates and populations of particle species.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from prior experimental results.

claim: The mean 2DTM SNR of detected targets provides a read-out of the relative similarity between different templates and populations of particle species.
source: This demonstrated that (1) 2DTM using partially matching templates can be sufficiently sensitive to yield significant targets and (2) the mean 2DTM SNR of detected targets provides a read-out of the relative similarity between different templates and populations of particle species.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from prior experimental results.

claim: 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis intermediates are of a similar size and share significant structure with one another, making them difficult to separate at low resolution.
source: As a model system, we chose to examine the late stages of 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae because (1) intermediates are of a similar size and share significant structure with one another, making them difficult to separate at low resolution, (2) molecular models spanning multiple late intermediate states have recently been described, and (3) the maturation events that occur before and after nuclear export have been characterized.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about 60S ribosome biogenesis.

claim: Molecular models spanning multiple late intermediate states of 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis have recently been described.
source: As a model system, we chose to examine the late stages of 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae because (1) intermediates are of a similar size and share significant structure with one another, making them difficult to separate at low resolution, (2) molecular models spanning multiple late intermediate states have recently been described, and (3) the maturation events that occur before and after nuclear export have been characterized.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about available structural models.

claim: The maturation events of 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis that occur before and after nuclear export have been characterized.
source: As a model system, we chose to examine the late stages of 60S ribosomal subunit biogenesis in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae because (1) intermediates are of a similar size and share significant structure with one another, making them difficult to separate at low resolution, (2) molecular models spanning multiple late intermediate states have recently been described, and (3) the maturation events that occur before and after nuclear export have been characterized.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about 60S ribosome biogenesis.

claim: Subcellular localization can validate the assignment of intermediate and mature states of 60S ribosomal subunits.
source: Subcellular localization can thereby validate the assignment of intermediate and mature states.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the known biology of 60S maturation.

claim: 2DTM can locate and distinguish nuclear intermediates of 60S maturation in 2D cryo-EM images of focused ion beam (FIB)-milled yeast cells.
source: We show that 2DTM can locate and distinguish nuclear intermediates of 60S maturation in 2D cryo-EM images of focused ion beam (FIB)-milled yeast cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: 2DTM can distinguish predefined 60S populations separated by subcellular localization.
source: We confirm that 2DTM can distinguish predefined 60S populations separated by subcellular localization and identify compositional differences between them.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: 2DTM can identify compositional differences between 60S populations.
source: We confirm that 2DTM can distinguish predefined 60S populations separated by subcellular localization and identify compositional differences between them.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A maximum likelihood-based approach can identify two sub-populations of nuclear intermediates that were not otherwise separable.
source: We apply a maximum likelihood-based approach to identify two sub-populations of nuclear intermediates that were not otherwise separable and provide a confidence of single particle classification.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A maximum likelihood-based approach can provide a confidence of single particle classification.
source: We apply a maximum likelihood-based approach to identify two sub-populations of nuclear intermediates that were not otherwise separable and provide a confidence of single particle classification.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methodology described in Figure 3.

claim: The nuclear pre-60S intermediate population shifts to a more mature intermediate after inhibiting Crm1-mediated nuclear export.
source: We show that using this approach, we can observe a shift in the nuclear pre-60S intermediate population to a more mature intermediate after inhibiting Crm1-mediated nuclear export.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Different particle populations in cells can be modelled with a Gaussian distribution of their relative 2DTM SNR ratios to effectively distinguish related complexes.
source: This study demonstrates that different particle populations in cells can be modelled with a Gaussian distribution of their relative 2DTM SNR ratios to effectively distinguish related complexes and identify population changes in cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methodology and results presented in Figures 3 and 6.

claim: Gaussian distribution of relative 2DTM SNR ratios can identify population changes in cells.
source: This study demonstrates that different particle populations in cells can be modelled with a Gaussian distribution of their relative 2DTM SNR ratios to effectively distinguish related complexes and identify population changes in cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing changes after Crm1 inhibition.

claim: 2DTM identified 4363 large ribosomal subunits in 28 2D cryo-EM images of the nuclear periphery of 7 lamellae generated from actively growing Sacchromyces cerevisiae cells.
source: We identified 4363 large ribosomal subunits by 2DTM using a template generated from a model representing the mature 60S (PDB: 6Q8Y) (Tesina et al., 2019; Figure 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The peaks corresponding to significant detections were clearly distinguishable from background.
source: The peaks corresponding to significant detections were clearly distinguishable from background (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), enabling precise localization of mature 60S in the cell.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D, E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 2DTM enables precise localization of mature 60S in the cell.
source: The peaks corresponding to significant detections were clearly distinguishable from background (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), enabling precise localization of mature 60S in the cell.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: No significant mature 60S-detected targets were observed in regions of the image corresponding to the vacuole.
source: Consistent with the expected high specificity of 2DTM, we did not observe any significant mature 60S-detected targets in regions of the image corresponding to the vacuole (Figure 1C and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and G.

claim: 229 mature 60S-detected targets localized to the nucleus, representing ~5% of all mature 60S identified targets.
source: In contrast, 229 mature 60S-detected targets localized to the nucleus, representing ~5% of all mature 60S identified targets in these images, well above the expected one false positive per image (Figure 1C–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The number of nuclear mature 60S-detected targets is well above the expected one false positive per image.
source: In contrast, 229 mature 60S-detected targets localized to the nucleus, representing ~5% of all mature 60S identified targets in these images, well above the expected one false positive per image (Figure 1C–G).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of observed detections with expected false positive rate.

claim: The normalized maximum intensity projections (MIPs) have a distribution of values similar in shape and location of their maxima in different regions of the image, corresponding to the nucleus, cytoplasm, and vacuole.
source: We found that the normalized maximum intensity projections (MIPs) have a distribution of values similar in shape and location of their maxima in different regions of the image, corresponding to the nucleus, cytoplasm, and vacuole.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The probability of false positives is similar in different compartments (nucleus, cytoplasm, vacuole).
source: This indicates that the probability of a false positives is also similar in these different compartments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-E).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the similarity of MIP distributions.

claim: The slight differences in the MIP distributions between the compartments likely result from differences in their composition.
source: The slight differences in the MIP distributions between the compartments likely result from differences in their composition.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the cause of observed differences.

claim: False detections are not more likely in visibly darker or denser regions of the image.
source: We conclude that false detections are not more likely in visibly darker or denser regions of the image.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the MIP distribution analysis.

claim: The median density of 60S in the cytoplasm is ~6500 60S/μm3.
source: In regions of the images corresponding to the cytoplasm we observe a median density of ~6500 60S/μm3, which, assuming an average cell volume of ~42 μm3 of which ~65% is cytoplasm, corresponds to a total of ~180,000 60S/cell (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The observed cytoplasmic 60S density corresponds to a total of ~180,000 60S/cell.
source: In regions of the images corresponding to the cytoplasm we observe a median density of ~6500 60S/μm3, which, assuming an average cell volume of ~42 μm3 of which ~65% is cytoplasm, corresponds to a total of ~180,000 60S/cell (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is based on calculation from observed density and assumed cell volume.

claim: The estimated total of ~180,000 60S/cell is consistent with prior estimates of 187,000 ± 56,000 ribosomes per yeast cell based on rRNA concentration.
source: This is consistent with prior estimates of 187,000 ± 56,000 ribosomes per yeast cell based on rRNA concentration (von der Haar, 2008).
evidence: The claim compares the current results with prior published estimates (von der Haar, 2008).

claim: The median density of 60S in the nucleus was ~30-fold lower than in the cytoplasm at ~200 60S/µm3.
source: The median density in the nucleus was ~30-fold lower at ~200 60S/µm3 (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The lower density of 60S particles in the nucleus agrees with previously observed lower density of 60S particles in the nucleus.
source: This agrees with the previously observed lower density of 60S particles in the nucleus, e.g. (Delavoie et al., 2019), but likely only reflects a subset of the nuclear 60S population.
evidence: The claim compares current results with prior observations (Delavoie et al., 2019).

claim: The observed nuclear 60S density likely only reflects a subset of the nuclear 60S population.
source: This agrees with the previously observed lower density of 60S particles in the nucleus, e.g. (Delavoie et al., 2019), but likely only reflects a subset of the nuclear 60S population.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the completeness of detection.

claim: Mature 60S-detected targets were oriented with their polypeptide exit tunnels facing the cytoplasmic surface of the nuclear envelope.
source: We found that mature 60S-detected targets were oriented with their polypeptide exit tunnels facing the cytoplasmic surface of the NE but were depleted from within ~20 nm of the vacuole (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: Mature 60S-detected targets were depleted from within ~20 nm of the vacuole.
source: We found that mature 60S-detected targets were oriented with their polypeptide exit tunnels facing the cytoplasmic surface of the NE but were depleted from within ~20 nm of the vacuole (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: The orientation of 60S identified by 2DTM is unlikely to be an artefact introduced by features of the membrane in the image.
source: This indicates that the orientation of 60S identified by 2DTM is unlikely to be an artefact introduced by features of the membrane in the image.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the biologically relevant orientations observed.

claim: A 3D reconstruction generated using the locations and orientations of 3991 significant mature 60S-detected targets shows density reminiscent of the 40S small ribosomal subunit in addition to the 60S.
source: To confirm that the targets identified with the mature 60S template reflect ribosomes, we generated a 3D reconstruction using the locations and orientations of 3991 significant mature 60S-detected targets using standard single particle approaches as described previously (Lucas et al., 2021). In addition to the 60S, the 10 Å-filtered reconstruction shows density reminiscent of the 40S small ribosomal subunit (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The presence of 40S density in the reconstruction is consistent with many of the mature 60S detected targets representing a population of 80S ribosomes.
source: This is consistent with many of the mature 60S detected targets representing a population of 80S ribosomes.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observed 40S density.

claim: The resolution of the 40S is lower relative to the 60S in the reconstruction.
source: Local resolution estimation shows that the resolution of the 40S is lower relative to the 60S (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The lower resolution of the 40S follows the expected positional heterogeneity of the 40S relative to the 60S when capturing ribosomes in a range of translation states.
source: This follows the expected positional heterogeneity of the 40S relative to the 60S when capturing ribosomes in a range of translation states (Freitas et al., 2021; Korostelev, 2022) and prior results using 50S Mycoplasma pneumoniae targets (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is based on inference supported by citations to prior work (Freitas et al., 2021; Korostelev, 2022; Lucas et al., 2021).

claim: 2DTM-identified locations and orientations in 2D cryo-EM images of FIB-milled lamellae reflect biologically relevant locations and orientations of ribosomes in the cell.
source: We conclude that 2DTM-identified locations and orientations in 2D cryo-EM images of FIB-milled lamellae reflect biologically relevant locations and orientations of ribosomes in the cell.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple lines of evidence presented in Figure 1.

claim: The nuclear envelope (NE) creates a physical barrier that separates premature 60S in the nucleus from mature 60S in the cytoplasm.
source: The nuclear envelope (NE) creates a physical barrier that separates premature 60S in the nucleus from mature 60S in the cytoplasm and is easily distinguishable in many 2D images by its characteristic double membrane and by the more granular appearance of the cytoplasm vs the nucleus (e.g. Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: The nuclear envelope is easily distinguishable in many 2D images by its characteristic double membrane and by the more granular appearance of the cytoplasm vs the nucleus.
source: The nuclear envelope (NE) creates a physical barrier that separates premature 60S in the nucleus from mature 60S in the cytoplasm and is easily distinguishable in many 2D images by its characteristic double membrane and by the more granular appearance of the cytoplasm vs the nucleus (e.g. Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1B.

claim: The nuclear 60S detected with the mature 60S template may result from cross-detection of nuclear precursors, which share part of their structure with mature 60S.
source: Our observation of a substantial population of mature 60S-detected targets in the nucleus, but not in the vacuole (Figure 1C and G), suggests that the nuclear 60S may result from cross-detection of nuclear precursors, which share part of their structure with mature 60S and therefore also produce significant correlations (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on observed data.

claim: The LN 60S represents the most mature nuclear intermediate for which there is a structure.
source: The LN 60S was chosen because it represents the most mature nuclear intermediate for which there is a structure, and which retains ribosome biogenesis factors (RBFs) that are removed during nuclear and early cytoplasmic processing (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about available structures.

claim: The LN 60S retains ribosome biogenesis factors (RBFs) that are removed during nuclear and early cytoplasmic processing.
source: The LN 60S was chosen because it represents the most mature nuclear intermediate for which there is a structure, and which retains ribosome biogenesis factors (RBFs) that are removed during nuclear and early cytoplasmic processing (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about 60S maturation.

claim: The similarities between the mature 60S and LN 60S structures will result in cross-detection of the respective other complex.
source: Thus, we expect that (1) the similarities between the mature 60S and LN 60S structures will result in cross-detection of the respective other complex and (2) the cytoplasmic population will more closely resemble the mature 60S and nuclear population will more closely resemble the LN 60S resulting in a higher mature 60S / LN 60S 2DTM SNR ratio in the cytoplasm than the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the structural similarity of the templates.

claim: The cytoplasmic population will more closely resemble the mature 60S and nuclear population will more closely resemble the LN 60S resulting in a higher mature 60S / LN 60S 2DTM SNR ratio in the cytoplasm than the nucleus.
source: Thus, we expect that (1) the similarities between the mature 60S and LN 60S structures will result in cross-detection of the respective other complex and (2) the cytoplasmic population will more closely resemble the mature 60S and nuclear population will more closely resemble the LN 60S resulting in a higher mature 60S / LN 60S 2DTM SNR ratio in the cytoplasm than the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the known biology of 60S maturation.

claim: 1651 significant LN 60S-detected targets were located in 28 images of the nucleus and nuclear periphery.
source: In the 28 images of the nucleus and nuclear periphery we located 1651 significant LN 60S-detected targets of which 1382 (~84%) of the LN 60S-detected targets were cytoplasmic and 268 (16%) were nuclear, a three-fold greater proportion than the mature 60S-detected targets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 1382 (~84%) of the LN 60S-detected targets were cytoplasmic and 268 (16%) were nuclear.
source: In the 28 images of the nucleus and nuclear periphery we located 1651 significant LN 60S-detected targets of which 1382 (~84%) of the LN 60S-detected targets were cytoplasmic and 268 (16%) were nuclear, a three-fold greater proportion than the mature 60S-detected targets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The proportion of nuclear LN 60S-detected targets is three-fold greater than the mature 60S-detected targets.
source: In the 28 images of the nucleus and nuclear periphery we located 1651 significant LN 60S-detected targets of which 1382 (~84%) of the LN 60S-detected targets were cytoplasmic and 268 (16%) were nuclear, a three-fold greater proportion than the mature 60S-detected targets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of experimental data.

claim: More cytoplasmic than nuclear targets were identified in 2DTM searches with both mature and LN 60S templates because the cytoplasm represented a larger area of the images.
source: We identified more cytoplasmic than nuclear targets in 2DTM searches with both mature and LN 60S templates because (1) the cytoplasm represented a larger area of our images and (2) the concentration of 60S is expected to be higher in the cytoplasm relative to the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental design.

claim: More cytoplasmic than nuclear targets were identified in 2DTM searches with both mature and LN 60S templates because the concentration of 60S is expected to be higher in the cytoplasm relative to the nucleus.
source: We identified more cytoplasmic than nuclear targets in 2DTM searches with both mature and LN 60S templates because (1) the cytoplasm represented a larger area of our images and (2) the concentration of 60S is expected to be higher in the cytoplasm relative to the nucleus.
evidence: The claim is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: Only one of the significant LN 60S-detected targets localized to the vacuole, which is below the expected false positive rate.
source: Only one of the significant LN 60S-detected targets localized to the vacuole, which is below the expected false positive rate and further indicates the specificity of 2DTM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and comparison with expected false positive rate.

claim: The low number of LN 60S-detected targets in the vacuole further indicates the specificity of 2DTM.
source: Only one of the significant LN 60S-detected targets localized to the vacuole, which is below the expected false positive rate and further indicates the specificity of 2DTM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the low false positive rate.

claim: The locations of many of the targets identified in the mature and LN 60S searches overlap.
source: As expected from the similarity between the mature and LN 60S templates, the locations of many of the targets identified in the two searches overlap (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Approximately one third of the mature 60S-detected targets overlapped with LN 60S-detected targets.
source: Approximately one third of the mature 60S-detected targets overlapped with LN 60S-detected targets while 92% of the LN 60S-detected targets overlapped with mature 60S-detected targets (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: 92% of the LN 60S-detected targets overlapped with mature 60S-detected targets.
source: Approximately one third of the mature 60S-detected targets overlapped with LN 60S-detected targets while 92% of the LN 60S-detected targets overlapped with mature 60S-detected targets (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: 30% of the nuclear targets were LN 60S-detected only, compared to only 0.5% of the cytoplasmic targets.
source: Combining the results of both searches, 30% of the nuclear targets were LN 60S-detected only, compared to only 0.5% of the cytoplasmic targets (Figure 2I, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The median log2(mature 60S / LN 60S 2DTM SNR) values of targets identified with both templates were significantly higher for the cytoplasmic population than the nuclear population (P<0.0001, K-S. test).
